header: Date: 2026-06-02 11:00 PT | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Gutierrez (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Venator Head of ML), Priya Singh (Eng Manager), Jordan Blake (CTO)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today, i'm Maya from Redwood, joining with Carlos our solutions engineer. quick intro round.
[00:08] Alex: Alex here, head of ML at Venator — thanks. we want to scope a short POC to validate cost and latency for our enrichment pipeline.
[00:15] Priya: priya — eng manager, we'll own integration, mainly node/k8s based.
[00:20] Jordan: Jordan, CTO — interested in cost and compliance, esp. private deployment options.
[00:28] Carlos: great, rough agenda: confirm success criteria, walk workload, run through cost model levers (per-token, batching, caching, quant), and agree bench/timeline.
[00:37] Alex: high level — we have a streaming enrichment job, ~150 reqs/sec peak, avg prompt 220 tokens, avg generated tokens 120. latency SLO is 350ms p50, want <800ms p95. monthly budget target is $12k for inference.
[00:55] Maya: okay good. quick clarification — are those 150 rps sustained or spiky bursts?
[01:00] Alex: it's spiky, think 10-15 minute bursts, usually 10k events/hour during peaks. we can shape traffic for POC but want representative spikes.
[01:12] Carlos: note — bursts change batching behavior; continuous batching benefits more if you have steady stream, spikes may lower effective batch sizes. we'll take that into account in bench.
[01:20] Priya: also, we have PII in some inputs, need encryption at rest and KMS integration, also SSO for admin UI.
[01:27] Maya: yep we will share security docs SOC2/KMS steps. Private deployment is possible but tends to add overhead/time; we'll quantify.
[01:35] Jordan: budget constraint is firm — $12k/month for inference, excluding data storage. want to know if hosted can meet perf and budget or if dedicated/reserved capacity is required.
[01:44] Carlos: ok let's walk through unit economics. baseline assumptions: model family: large open model (70B-class quantized) — for planning we use an example gen cost of $0.10 per 1k output tokens and $0.02 per 1k input tokens on hosted; this is a planning number — final will come by model selection. those numbers reflect our hosted SKU with mid-range GPU.
[02:05] Alex: per 1k tokens, can you remind how that maps to our traffic?
[02:09] Carlos: sure. at avg prompt 220 tokens and 120 generated, that's 340 tokens per request. at 150 req/sec sustained that is 51,000 tokens/sec => ~4.4 billion tokens/day — obviously you don't sustain that continuously; for a month a more typical blended number for you (we estimate) is 1.2B tokens/month given spike patterns you described. multiply by per-1k price: 1.2B tokens /1k * $0.10 = $120,000/month (naive).
[02:40] Alex: whoa that is way above budget. where are the levers?
[02:44] Carlos: several levers — batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization (4-bit), model choice (smaller distil variant), and routing to cheaper model for lower-confidence prompts. with batching and continuous prefix cache for repeated context we can cut token compute by 20-60% depending on reuse. quantization and optimized runtime can drop compute costs 2-3x. we also suggest a hybrid: use smaller faster model for majority and fall back to larger one for complex QA.
[03:10] Priya: can you show a concrete example that gets to $12k?
[03:14] Carlos: yes — realistic POC config: 1) use a distilled 13-20B variant for most calls with $0.03/1k gen + $0.01/1k input equivalent. 2) apply prefix caching on repeated enrichment keys — expected cache hit 40% (you said many events share user profile snippets) which reduces effective tokens by 35% on average. 3) enable batching with target batch window 20ms for spikes which raises throughput and reduces GPU idle. combined effect — blended effective tokens per req drops to ~220 effective tokens. with pricing that maps to ~0.22k tokens/request => monthly tokens ~220 * requests/month. if we assume your blended throughput is 200M tokens/month -> cost ~200M/1k * $0.04 = $8,000. that's within budget with margin for data transfer.
[03:58] Alex: ok those look promising — a couple of questions: how do batching windows impact latency? and what's the risk of quality loss with smaller model?
[04:08] Carlos: batching window tradeoff — with 20ms batching target we see minor added tail latency for single requests but big throughput gains. in prior benches on similar workloads we hit p50 180-260ms and p95 around 450-650ms depending on model and cache hits. Quality: smaller model may introduce regressions; we recommend an eval set (we'll help build) and we can run A/B: 85% traffic to small model, 15% to large to catch regressions.
[04:36] Priya: for the POC we need a bench plan and specific success criteria. what do you propose?
[04:41] Maya: proposed success criteria on our side: 1) cost target: < $12k/mo equivalent at production scale using recommended knobs, 2) latency SLO: p50 <350ms p95 <800ms on blended traffic, 3) quality: no more than 5% drop on key eval metrics vs your current baseline. if those meet, we recommend moving to a 3-month pilot.
[05:05] Alex: agreed to those three; we'll provide a baseline eval suite and traffic sample.
[05:10] Carlos: bench plan: week 1 — integration (API keys, network rules, sample traffic mapping). week 2 — synthetic bench: run steady-state and burst tests, measure batch sizes, latencies, token throughput, and cost-per-1k observed. week 3 — live pilot with 1-2% of production traffic for 1 week, collect metrics. week 4 — analyze results, tuning, handoff. we'll produce a cost model spreadsheet with scenario toggles (cache hit rate, quantization level, model splits).
[05:39] Jordan: how long for Dedicated or Private deployment to be available if we opt for that?
[05:44] Maya: Dedicated reserved pools typically take 4-6 weeks to provision for new customers; Private (VPC/on-prem) is 8-12 weeks depending on network approvals and compliance. POC can run on Hosted to validate economics faster.
[05:56] Alex: what about pricing for reserved? sometimes reserved gives better unit cost right?
[05:59] Carlos: yes reserved/Dedicated reduces unit compute cost by ~20-40% on committed capacity; exact depends on GPU type and commitment length. our cost model spreadsheet will include reserved vs on-demand comparison.
[06:10] Priya: any gotchas with KV cache in our architecture? we store per-user small context in redis today. we want to avoid extra hop latency.
[06:18] Carlos: good question — we support colocated KV caching inside the runtime for hot keys which avoids roundtrips and gives <1ms added overhead; for cold keys you can rely on your redis layer. we'll show both patterns in bench.
[06:28] Alex: about data residency and logs — do you retain logs by default? we need audit logs offsite retention for compliance.
[06:35] Maya: default retention is 30 days, we have enterprise options for longer retentions and exportable audit logs, plus KMS for encryption. we'll attach SOC2 summary in follow up.
[06:45] Priya: okay, on instrumentation what metrics do you export? we need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, per-model traces.
[06:53] Carlos: Redwood Console exposes token counts, token-cost breakdown by request id, per-model route dashboards, and trace hooks. We'll make sure your eval events are tagged so you can slice cost by route.
[07:02] Alex: for the bench run — what do you need from us to set it up?
[07:06] Carlos: sample traffic (1 day of anonymized events), expected concurrency profile, eval prompt set (50-200 examples with pass/fail metrics), and network allowlist for testing.
[07:15] Alex: we'll produce that by next Thursday.
[07:18] Maya: perfect. final note on cost model: we'll include sensitivity knobs — cache hit rate (10-70%), batching window (0-50ms), quantization (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and model split percentage. we'll produce three scenarios: conservative, target, and aggressive with cost projections.
[07:36] Jordan: sounds good. one last question — do you have live examples of customers with similar workload and budgets?
[07:41] Maya: yes — we have a retail analytics customer who used a 13B distill + caching approach and hit similar budget targets; we can share an anonymized case study.
[07:50] Alex: ok thanks, that helps.
[07:52] Maya: recap of next steps — we'll send the cost model spreadsheet, SOC2 and KMS docs, and Carlos will run the synthetic bench once traffic samples arrive. Alex will provide traffic and eval set. action items recorded in the doc.
[08:05] Priya: thanks everyone, looking forward to the POC.
[08:08] Carlos: thanks all.
[08:10] [call end]
notes: Transcription includes typical ASR noise: product names and acronyms occasionally mis-transcribed. Conversation focused heavily on unit economics; Redwood recommended a hybrid approach (smaller model + fallbacks) + caching to meet the $12k target. POC timeline 4 weeks, bench to start after traffic sample.
